Choosing and interpreting a meddecide analysis

Source: vignettes/17-methods-and-interpretation.Rmd
17-methods-and-interpretation.Rmd

Choose the question before the statistic

Question Analysis Main condition or limitation
How accurate is one binary test? decision Specify both reference and test levels; the reference must support an accuracy claim.
What follows from four diagnostic counts? decisioncalculator Counts must describe the same population and reference; uncertainty in an externally supplied prevalence is not automatically propagated.
How do two tests combine under assumed accuracy? cotest Dependence is specified separately within disease groups; an arbitrary dependence value is not an estimate from paired observations.
What is the workload of a two-stage strategy? sequentialtests Combined accuracy assumes conditional independence. Entered accuracy, prevalence and costs are treated as fixed inputs.
How do observed combinations perform? decisioncombine Uses observed paired patterns, rather than multiplying marginal accuracies. Single-test rows use cases complete across selected tests.
Do tests differ on the same patients? decisioncompare Paired comparisons use the relevant complete pairs; per-test estimates can have different denominators. Independent rows are required.
What can imperfect tests tell us without a reference? nogoldstandard Latent methods require at least three tests; self-built reference rules describe agreement rather than diagnostic accuracy.
Which marker discriminates and at which cutpoint? enhancedROC AUC does not measure calibration; selected cutpoints have apparent performance. Frozen-model validation needs a locked model and appropriate validation data.
How do ROC markers or cutpoint methods compare? psychopdaROC Fix outcome coding and direction; patient summaries require a consistent outcome within patient. NRI/IDI based on probabilities require appropriate probability inputs.
Does a risk-based action improve net benefit? decisioncurve Supply risks on a 0–1 scale for a defined binary outcome and horizon. This analysis does not handle censoring.
How can predictors be combined? lassologistic Penalized coefficients have no conventional coefficient p-values here. Penalty selection by CV and performance validation are separate steps.
How reproducible are ratings? agreement Choose categorical, ordinal or continuous methods to match the scale and study design. Agreement with a rater does not establish accuracy against disease.
How many subjects for expected kappa limits? kappaSizeCI Confidence-limit planning, without a hypothesis test or a power guarantee.
How many subjects to test a null kappa? kappaSizePower Two-sided goodness-of-fit test under the common-correlation model; approximation and achieved-power warnings matter.
What lower kappa limit is expected with fixed N? kappaSizeFixedN Expected one-sided confidence bound, rather than power or a guaranteed minimum observed kappa.

Diagnostic accuracy and prevalence

With TP, FN, FP and TN denoting the four cells, sensitivity is TP/(TP+FN), specificity is TN/(TN+FP), and observed PPV is TP/(TP+FP). At target prevalence pp, transporting sensitivity SeSe and specificity SpSp gives

PPV(p)=SepSep+(1−Sp)(1−p),NPV(p)=Sp(1−p)Sp(1−p)+(1−Se)p.PPV(p)=\frac{Se\,p}{Se\,p+(1-Sp)(1-p)},\qquad NPV(p)=\frac{Sp(1-p)}{Sp(1-p)+(1-Se)p}.

Transport also assumes these accuracy estimates apply to the target population. Changing prevalence cannot repair spectrum bias, incorporation bias or selective verification. A ratio with denominator zero is undefined. Zero-cell handling for likelihood ratios is method-specific; read the displayed correction note.

se <- 0.80; sp <- 0.90; p <- 0.01
c(PPV = se*p/(se*p+(1-sp)*(1-p)),
  NPV = sp*(1-p)/(sp*(1-p)+(1-se)*p))
#>        PPV        NPV 
#> 0.07476636 0.99776036

Here a positive test has a predictive value of about 7.5%, despite 80% sensitivity and 90% specificity. A false-positive rate of 10% applies to people without disease; it is not the probability that a positive result is false.

The diagnostic analyses do not all use the same interval construction. Exact Clopper–Pearson and Wilson intervals can legitimately differ for the same proportion. Select the same population, coding, denominator and interval method before comparing outputs. cotest() and sequentialtests() accept prevalence from 0.001 to 0.999; very rare-disease scenarios outside that range are refused. decisioncompare() refuses simultaneous population-prevalence adjustment and confidence intervals; it does not supply transported uncertainty for that combination. Repeated observations require analysis at the patient level or a method that accounts for clustering.

Combining tests

Under conditional independence, an AND rule has sensitivity Se1Se2Se_1Se_2 and specificity 1−(1−Sp1)(1−Sp2)1-(1-Sp_1)(1-Sp_2). An OR rule has sensitivity 1−(1−Se1)(1−Se2)1-(1-Se_1)(1-Se_2) and specificity Sp1Sp2Sp_1Sp_2. These are conditional on disease status; an unconditional correlation between the two tests does not establish the needed assumption. Use observed paired patterns when available, and sensitivity analysis when dependence is uncertain.

ROC analysis and prediction

AUC measures rank discrimination. AUC 0.5 does not establish that a marker has no possible clinical use, and broad adjectives such as “excellent” are not clinical acceptance thresholds. Check uncertainty, direction, calibration and the consequences of errors. Youden’s index weights sensitivity and specificity equally and does not incorporate prevalence or clinical costs.

Optimizing a cutpoint and reporting its sensitivity on the same data is development. Bootstrap intervals around apparent performance do not automatically remove selection optimism. Lock the model, preprocessing, outcome definition, prediction horizon and threshold before independent validation.

For LASSO, the displayed training AUC remains apparent even when cross-validation selected lambda. Bootstrap optimism correction can leave residual optimism, especially with model and penalty selection in modest samples. It is internal validation and does not validate a simplified points score or a new clinical population. Penalized odds ratios describe shrunk model coefficients, rather than causal effects.

Decision curves

At threshold probability tt,

NB(t)=TP/n−FP/n×t/(1−t).NB(t)=TP/n-FP/n\times t/(1-t).

Treat-none has NB zero; treat-all has NB p−(1−p)t/(1−t)p-(1-p)t/(1-t). The threshold represents the relative consequences of a false positive and a true positive. Choose a clinically defensible range before looking at the curves. Do not feed an uncalibrated score as though it were a risk. Net benefit here uses the observed event fraction. A case-control sampling fraction is not a population event rate; this analysis has no prevalence-weighting correction for that design. A warning based on an outcome ratio cannot identify every case-control sample.

# 100 independent patients; at t=0.20 a model identifies 15 events and 20 non-events.
t <- 0.20
c(model = 15/100 - 20/100*t/(1-t),
  treat_all = 0.20 - 0.80*t/(1-t), treat_none = 0)
#>         model     treat_all    treat_none 
#>  1.000000e-01 -2.775558e-17  0.000000e+00

The model’s net benefit is 0.10 per patient under these utilities. This does not mean ten lives saved per 100 patients. Interventions avoided are a utility-scaled comparison with treat-all, rather than a measured clinical outcome. A pointwise interval clearing the treat-all estimate is not a paired test of their difference.

The definition follows Vickers and Elkin (2006).

Agreement and study size

Kappa depends on the marginal category frequencies. Weighted kappa also depends on the order and weights assigned to categories. ICC needs a stated model, agreement/consistency target, and single/average-measure estimand. Correlation alone does not measure agreement, and Bland–Altman limits describe differences on the measurement scale.

The three kappa planners assume a common-correlation, common-margin rating model. With two raters and equal margins its kappa coincides with Cohen’s kappa; unequal rater margins, weighted kappa, missing ratings and clustered specimens need design-specific planning. Increasing the number of raters does not simply multiply the number of independent subjects.

Function Meaning of kappa0 What the result provides
kappaSizeCI Anticipated kappa N needed for specified expected goodness-of-fit confidence limits
kappaSizeFixedN Anticipated kappa Expected one-sided lower confidence bound at fixed N
kappaSizePower Null kappa N for a two-sided test against alternative kappa1

The realized confidence interval varies between studies. Planning its expected limits does not guarantee that a future interval lies inside those limits. Read the kappaSize reference manual and the module’s approximation and sparse-cell notes; confirm demanding designs by simulation of the analysis you intend to use.

Without a gold standard

Two latent classes are unlabeled. A high-positive class is not automatically disease. With three binary tests there are seven independent response-pattern probabilities and seven model parameters: one class proportion and six response probabilities. Such a model has zero residual degrees of freedom. A good fit or non-significant residual check therefore cannot establish conditional independence. Extra tests permit some checks but do not prove the assumption.

The method named bayesian in R is fixed-prior penalized EM/MAP point estimation. It does not sample a posterior; bootstrap confidence intervals are not posterior credible intervals. Reference rules that include the evaluated test have incorporation bias and provide agreement with that rule, not disease accuracy.

See the worked example and a simulation study of dependence diagnostics.

What to report

Report the source population, independent observation unit, reference and outcome coding, exclusions, missingness, model or threshold provenance, estimator and interval method, uncertainty, and whether performance is apparent, internally validated or independently validated. Teaching scenarios and simulated data illustrate the calculation; they do not supply clinical recommendations.
